subject: Biotechnology
title: The Science of GMO Safety
description: Learn The Science of GMO Safety in one minute.

hook.text: Are GMOs safe? Over 2,000 studies say yes — the scientific consensus is overwhelming, yet public doubt persists.

buildup.text: The National Academies, WHO, and European Commission reviewed decades of evidence — no health risks from approved GMO foods.

discovery.text: Substantial equivalence compares GMOs to conventional counterparts — if nutritionally identical, no extra testing is required.

twist.text: The Séralini study claimed GMO corn caused tumors in rats — but it was retracted for poor methodology and small sample size.

climax.text: Anti-GMO sentiment is driven more by distrust in corporations than by scientific evidence — perception gaps shape policy.

punchline.text: Science says safe, society says maybe — the GMO debate is about trust, not toxicology.

quiz.question: Why was the Séralini study on GMO corn retracted?
options: The study proved GMOs were safe, contradicting the authors' claims
Poor methodology and insufficient sample sizes made the conclusions unreliable
The rats in the study were a species immune to cancer

details.summary: Thousands of studies and decades of consumption data support the safety of approved GM foods. Major scientific bodies including the WHO, National Academies, and EFSA conclude that GM foods on the market are as safe as their conventional counterparts.
details.whyItMatters: Scientific consensus on GMO safety is one of the strongest in modern biology, yet public perception often diverges. Bridging this gap is essential for evidence-based food policy and for realizing the benefits of agricultural biotechnology.
takeaways: Over 3,000 studies confirm no health risks unique to approved GM foods
Every major scientific organization affirms the safety of approved GM foods
GM foods undergo more safety testing than conventionally bred varieties

faq.question: Is there any credible scientific evidence that GM foods are harmful?
faq.answer: No. A comprehensive review of over 3,000 studies by the National Academies of Sciences found no evidence of health risks from approved GM foods. The Seralini study claiming GM corn caused tumors was retracted due to severe methodological flaws.

faq.question: How are GM foods tested before reaching consumers?
faq.answer: GM foods undergo compositional analysis, allergenicity testing, toxicology studies, nutritional assessment, and environmental impact review. The approval process typically takes 7 to 10 years and costs over 100 million dollars, far exceeding testing for conventional breeds.
